questions.subject: PHYSICS_II
questions.topic: Entropy as a count of arrangements
questions.learningObjective: Explain why entropy can be read as a logarithm of the count of arrangements
questions.stem: A graph of ln W against energy is shown. Explain in writing why entropy can be read off such a graph as a logarithm of the count of arrangements.

answer.exemplar: The multiplicity W counts the microscopic arrangements that share one macrostate, and Boltzmann's relation ties the entropy to that count through S = k ln W. Plotting ln W against energy therefore puts the entropy on the graph in units of k, and the steepest point of the curve marks the most probable macrostate, where the number of arrangements is largest.

questions.explanation: Boltzmann's relation S = k ln W connects entropy to the number of microscopic arrangements, so a plot of ln W is a plot of the entropy in units of k. Its maximum marks the most probable macrostate.
questions.hint: Entropy counts arrangements through a logarithm.

answer.exemplar: The number of arrangements compatible with a macrostate grows and then falls as the energy is varied, so the macrostate with the largest multiplicity is the one whose point on the ln W curve sits highest. questions.topic: Heat capacity as a count of degrees of freedom

questions.stem: Plotted for a solid, the graph of heat capacity against temperature rises to a plateau. Explain in writing how the heat capacity of a solid is related to the number of degrees of freedom of its atoms.

answer.exemplar: Each quadratic degree of freedom of an atom, such as one component of its kinetic energy or one coordinate of its vibration, contributes one half k to the heat capacity, so a solid whose atoms can move in three dimensions and vibrate in three directions reaches 3k per atom at high temperature. questions.explanation: The observed curve tells how many of the possible motions are actually excited at the temperature in view.
questions.hint: Each quadratic term contributes half of k.

questions.topic: What temperature corresponds to statistically
questions.learningObjective: Explain how a population ratio between two levels determines the temperature
questions.stem: A graph of populations against temperature is used to extract a temperature. Explain in writing how the population ratio of two levels determines the temperature.

answer.exemplar: For two levels separated by an energy gap E the ratio of their populations follows the Boltzmann factor, the ratio of the lower population to the upper one being the exponential of the gap divided by kT. Reading the ratio off the graph and taking its logarithm gives the gap divided by kT, and dividing that gap by the result yields the temperature. The measurement is statistical because it uses the balance of many particles rather than any single one.

questions.explanation: The balance of large numbers is what makes the temperature a statistical property of the sample rather than of one particle.
questions.hint: Take the logarithm of the population ratio.

answer.exemplar: A macrostate is specified by a few macroscopic variables, such as the total energy and the volume, and each such specification is compatible with a very large number of distinct microscopic arrangements because the particles can be distributed among their accessible states in innumerable ways. questions.subject: PHYSICS_II
questions.topic: Heat capacity as a count of degrees of freedom
questions.learningObjective: Explain why the heat capacity of a gas depends on temperature at fixed sample size
questions.stem: Explaining a temperature dependence, a graph of heat capacity against temperature for a gas shows why the heat capacity changes even when the amount of gas is fixed.

answer.exemplar: The heat capacity measures how much energy is needed to raise the temperature, and a gas can store energy in many different modes, not only in the translation of its centre of mass. At low temperature only the translational modes carry appreciable energy, so the heat capacity is low, while at higher temperature molecular rotations and then vibrations are excited and each newly active mode adds its own share to the heat capacity. That is why the curve of heat capacity against temperature rises in steps even though the quantity of gas never changes.

questions.explanation: The temperature dependence is a change in the modes available, not a change in the amount of gas present.
questions.hint: Newly excited modes add to the heat capacity.

questions.stem: A graph of the spread of state populations against temperature is used to define a temperature. Explain in writing how a broader or narrower population spread is read as a higher or lower temperature.

answer.exemplar: The Boltzmann factor suppresses high energy states more strongly when the temperature is low, so at low temperature the population is concentrated on the ground state and the distribution of populated levels is narrow. Raising the temperature populates more and more levels, the spread of the distribution broadens, and the ratio of any two populations moves closer to one. The temperature therefore controls how broadly the states are populated, and reading the width of that spread is a way of extracting the temperature from the data.

questions.explanation: The width of the spread is therefore a direct reading of the temperature from the population data.
questions.hint: Look at how broadly the states are populated.

answer.exemplar: Probability in statistical mechanics is assigned to the many microscopic arrangements rather than to the named macroscopic conditions, so a macrostate gathers together every arrangement that shares its macroscopic numbers. Each individual arrangement is only one of a huge collection, while the macrostate stands for all of them at once, and the probability assigned to the macrostate is the sum of the probabilities of the arrangements it contains. That is why the macrostate is the more probable object even though it is the less detailed description.
